Anatomy-1.question: ১) Mitochondrial Enzymes takes part in?
Anatomy-1.exp:
The mitochondria are the primary site of aerobic energy production. They contain enzymes involved in several essential metabolic processes:

  • Electron transport chain (ETC): Located on the inner mitochondrial membrane, where electrons are transferred through enzyme complexes.

  • Oxidative phosphorylation: Also occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane, where ATP is synthesized by ATP synthase using the proton gradient generated by the ETC.

  • Citric acid (Krebs/TCA) cycle: Takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, where enzymes generate NADH and FADH₂ for the electron transport chain.

Anatomy-1.question: ২) Which one is not true about Mitochondria?
Anatomy-1.option3: They are called power house of cell.
Anatomy-1.exp:
All three statements about mitochondria are correct:

  • Mitochondria can synthesize proteins using their own mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), ribosomes, and transfer RNAs. However, they synthesize only a small number of mitochondrial proteins; most are encoded by nuclear DNA.

  • They are self-replicating, dividing independently by binary fission.

  • They are known as the "powerhouse of the cell" because they generate the majority of cellular ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩) Which statement is not false?
Anatomy-1.option1: Rough Endoplasmic Reticulam produces serum protein
Anatomy-1.option2: Smoth ER are responsible for lipid metabolism
Anatomy-1.option3: Golgi apparatus helps in processing of newly synthesized proteins.
Anatomy-1.exp:
All three statements are correct:

  • Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) synthesizes secretory and membrane proteins, including most serum proteins in hepatocytes (except immunoglobulins, which are synthesized by plasma cells).

  • Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is responsible for lipid metabolism, steroid synthesis, and detoxification.

  • Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, packages, and processes newly synthesized proteins before they are transported to their final destinations.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪) Which statement is False?
Anatomy-1.option3: Ribosome has two sub unit -50S and 30 S.
Anatomy-1.exp:
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is not involved in protein synthesis. Its main functions include lipid and steroid synthesis, detoxification of drugs and toxins, carbohydrate metabolism, and calcium storage (especially in muscle cells).

The other statements are considered true in standard cell biology:

  • Lysosomes are called the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they contain hydrolytic enzymes capable of digesting cellular components.

  • Ribosomes consist of two subunits. Although 50S and 30S specifically refer to prokaryotic (70S) ribosomes, this statement is generally accepted in basic microbiology.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫) Regarding Ribosome which one is not true?
Anatomy-1.option3: Ribosomes attached with Endoplasmic Reticulum produce intra cytoplasmic protein.
Anatomy-1.exp:
All three statements are incorrect:

  • Membranous organelle – False. Ribosomes are non-membranous organelles composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.

  • Free ribosome produce exportable proteins – False. Free ribosomes synthesize proteins that function within the cytoplasm or are transported to organelles such as the nucleus and mitochondria.

  • Ribosomes attached with Endoplasmic Reticulum produce intra cytoplasmic protein – False. Ribosomes attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) synthesize secretory proteins, membrane proteins, and lysosomal proteins, not intracellular cytoplasmic proteins.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬) Which Statement is true?
Anatomy-1.option1: Centrosome give rise to motile cilia
Anatomy-1.exp:
All three statements are true:

  • Centrosome gives rise to motile cilia: The centrioles within the centrosome form basal bodies, which serve as the foundation for the development of motile cilia and flagella.

  • Microtubules assist in cellular movement: Microtubules are involved in intracellular transport, ciliary and flagellar movement, and chromosome separation during cell division.

  • Microfilaments participate in muscular contraction: Actin microfilaments interact with myosin to produce muscle contraction and are also involved in cell motility and cytokinesis.

Anatomy-1.question: ৭) Which one is not false?
Anatomy-1.option1: Eukaryotes contain single chromosome as genetic material.
Anatomy-1.exp:
Prokaryotes possess DNA, which serves as their genetic material. It is typically present as a single circular chromosome located in the nucleoid, and many prokaryotes also contain plasmids.

The other statements are false:

  • Eukaryotes contain single chromosome as genetic material – False. Eukaryotic cells contain multiple linear chromosomes enclosed within a nucleus.

  • Prokaryotes have cytoskeleton – Although modern research has identified cytoskeletal protein homologues in prokaryotes, in the context of standard undergraduate and medical textbooks, prokaryotes are classically considered to lack a true cytoskeleton. This statement is therefore regarded as false in most examinations.

  • Prokaryotes do not synthesize protein – False. Prokaryotes actively synthesize proteins using 70S ribosomes.

Anatomy-1.question: ৮) Which one is not true?
Anatomy-1.option1: Cell membrane lipids are of two types.
Anatomy-1.option3: Peripheral proteins of cell membrane act as enzyme.
Anatomy-1.exp:
The statement is false because cell membrane lipids are classically of three major types:

  • Phospholipids

  • Glycolipids

  • Cholesterol

The other statements are true:

  • Insulin receptors are integral (transmembrane) proteins with intrinsic tyrosine kinase activity.

  • Peripheral membrane proteins can function as enzymes, structural proteins, or signaling molecules.

Anatomy-1.question: ৯) Which one is not true as a true statement?
Anatomy-1.option1: Microtubules are the thinest of cytoskeletones.
Anatomy-1.option2: Desmin are the Intermediate filaments of muscle cell.
Anatomy-1.option3: Alfa and Beta are two sub unite of microtubules.
Anatomy-1.exp:
The statement is false because microtubules are the thickest component of the cytoskeleton, measuring about 25 nm in diameter. The thinnest cytoskeletal elements are the microfilaments (actin filaments), which are approximately 7 nm in diameter.

The other statements are true:

  • Desmin is the intermediate filament found in muscle cells, where it helps maintain structural integrity.

  • Microtubules are composed of α-tubulin and β-tubulin heterodimers, which polymerize to form the microtubule.

Anatomy-1.question: ১০) Which one is false?
Anatomy-1.option4: Zonulae Adherens are responsible for hearts coordinated beat.
Anatomy-1.exp:
The statement is false because the coordinated contraction of the heart depends on gap junctions, which allow the rapid passage of ions and electrical impulses between adjacent cardiac muscle cells. This electrical coupling enables the myocardium to function as a functional syncytium.

The other statements are true:

  • Tight junctions (zonula occludens) are impermeable and prevent the passage of substances through the intercellular space.

  • Desmosomes (macula adherens) are adhering junctions that provide strong mechanical attachment between cells.

  • Gap junctions are communicating junctions that permit direct intercellular exchange of ions and small molecules.

Anatomy-1.question: ১১) Function of Golgi apparatus-
Anatomy-1.exp:
The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages newly synthesized proteins and lipids into vesicles for secretion or delivery to their final intracellular destinations. It also plays a role in the formation of lysosomes.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • ATP production occurs in the mitochondria.

  • Protein synthesis is carried out by ribosomes, particularly those attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

  • mRNA synthesis (transcription) occurs in the nucleus.

Anatomy-1.question: ১২) Which one is non membranous organelle?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Ribosomes are non-membranous organelles composed of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins. They are the sites of protein synthesis and may be found free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

The other organelles are membrane-bound:

  • Golgi complex – Single membrane-bound organelle involved in protein modification and packaging.

  • Endoplasmic reticulum – Membrane-bound network responsible for protein and lipid synthesis.

  • Peroxisomes – Single membrane-bound organelles containing oxidative enzymes involved in fatty acid oxidation and detoxification.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৩) Which one is not function of cell membrane?
Anatomy-1.option1: Give a boundary to the cell.
Anatomy-1.option4: Serve as a site of receptor
Anatomy-1.exp:
The cell membrane does not produce ATP in eukaryotic cells. ATP is primarily synthesized in the mitochondria through oxidative phosphorylation. (In prokaryotes, ATP synthesis occurs across the plasma membrane because they lack mitochondria.)

The other options are normal functions of the cell membrane:

  • It forms the boundary of the cell and separates the intracellular from the extracellular environment.

  • It helps maintain the shape of the cell by interacting with the cytoskeleton.

  • It serves as a site for receptors involved in cell signaling, such as hormone and neurotransmitter receptors.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৪) Which protein is not found in cell membrane?
Anatomy-1.exp:
The cell membrane contains a variety of proteins that perform specialized functions, including:

  • Enzymes that catalyze membrane-associated biochemical reactions.

  • Transport proteins (channels, carriers, and pumps) that regulate the movement of substances across the membrane.

  • Structural proteins that anchor the cytoskeleton and maintain cell shape.

Plasma proteins (e.g., albumin, globulins, fibrinogen) are proteins present in the blood plasma, not structural components of the cell membrane.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৫) Which is not a Lysosomal Enzyme?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Lysosomes contain numerous acid hydrolases that digest intracellular and extracellular materials. These include:

  • Proteases – digest proteins.

  • Nucleases – digest DNA and RNA.

  • Esterases (including lipases) – hydrolyze ester bonds in lipids and other molecules.

Since all three enzymes are present in lysosomes, none of them is excluded.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৬) Which statement is not true?
Anatomy-1.option1: There are more then 30 nucleoporins in nucleus
Anatomy-1.option3: Transcription of mRNA ocurrs in nucleoplasm
Anatomy-1.exp:
Chromatin is classically divided into two types:

  • Euchromatin – loosely packed, transcriptionally active.

  • Heterochromatin – densely packed, transcriptionally inactive (or less active).

Therefore, the statement that chromatin is of three types is false.

The other statements are true:

  • More than 30 nucleoporins constitute the nuclear pore complex.

  • Transcription of mRNA occurs in the nucleoplasm by RNA polymerase II.

  • Nucleoplasm contains enzymes involved in DNA replication, transcription, and RNA processing.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৭) Mitochondria is not absent in?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Renal tubular cells contain a large number of mitochondria because they require substantial ATP for active transport during reabsorption of sodium, glucose, amino acids, and other solutes.

The other options lack mitochondria:

  • RBCs (erythrocytes) lose their mitochondria during maturation to maximize space for haemoglobin and avoid consuming oxygen.

  • Terminal keratinocytes (cells of the stratum corneum) are dead, fully keratinized cells and do not contain mitochondria.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৮) DNA synthesis occurs in?
Anatomy-1.exp:
DNA synthesis (DNA replication) occurs during the S (Synthesis) phase of the cell cycle. During this phase, each chromosome is duplicated to form two identical sister chromatids, ensuring that each daughter cell receives a complete set of genetic material during cell division.

The other phases have different functions:

  • G1 phase: Cell growth and synthesis of proteins and RNA.

  • G2 phase: Further cell growth and preparation for mitosis; DNA replication has already been completed.

  • G0 phase: A resting or quiescent phase in which the cell is metabolically active but does not divide.

Anatomy-1.question: ১৯) Period between two mitosis is called?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Interphase is the period between two successive mitotic divisions. It occupies about 90% of the cell cycle and is the phase during which the cell grows, replicates its DNA, and prepares for mitosis.

Interphase consists of:

  • G₁ phase – Cell growth and protein synthesis.

  • S phase – DNA replication.

  • G₂ phase – Preparation for mitosis.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Cell cycle includes both interphase and mitosis, so it is not merely the period between two mitoses.

  • G₂ phase is only one part of interphase.

  • Anaphase is a stage of mitosis.

Anatomy-1.question: ২০) Events of Interphase are?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Interphase is the period between two mitotic divisions and consists of three sequential phases:

  • G₁ (Gap 1) phase: Cell growth, synthesis of RNA and proteins, and preparation for DNA replication.

  • S (Synthesis) phase: DNA replication occurs, resulting in duplication of the chromosomes.

  • G₂ (Gap 2) phase: Further cell growth, synthesis of proteins required for mitosis, and preparation for cell division.

Anatomy-1.question: ২১) Which is not true regarding cell cycle duration?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Mitosis (M phase) is a relatively short phase, usually lasting about 1 hour in a typical mammalian cell. It does not take 24 hours.

Typical duration of the cell cycle is approximately 24 hours:

  • G₁ phase: ~10–12 hours (variable)

  • S phase: ~8 hours

  • G₂ phase: ~4 hours

  • M phase (mitosis): ~1 hour

Anatomy-1.question: ২২) Centrosome migrate to the pole of cell during-
Anatomy-1.exp:
During prophase, the duplicated centrosomes separate and migrate to opposite poles of the cell. As they move apart, they organize the mitotic spindle, which is essential for chromosome alignment and segregation.

The other phases occur after this event:

  • Metaphase: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.

  • Anaphase: Sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.

  • Telophase: Nuclear envelopes reform, and the spindle apparatus disassembles.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৩) Chromatid separates during-
Anatomy-1.exp:
During anaphase, the centromeres divide, allowing the sister chromatids to separate. Each chromatid is then pulled by the spindle fibers toward opposite poles of the cell, where it becomes an individual daughter chromosome.

The other phases have different roles:

  • Prophase: Chromosomes condense and the mitotic spindle forms.

  • Metaphase: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.

  • Telophase: Chromosomes reach the poles, decondense, and new nuclear envelopes are formed.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৪) Nuclei reappear during -
Anatomy-1.exp:
During telophase, the nuclear envelope re-forms around each set of daughter chromosomes, and the nucleoli reappear. At the same time, the chromosomes begin to decondense, and the mitotic spindle disassembles, marking the end of mitosis.

The other phases are characterized by:

  • Prophase: Nuclear envelope and nucleolus disappear.

  • Metaphase: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.

  • Anaphase: Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৫) Subdivision of prophase-1 are/is-
Anatomy-1.exp:
Prophase I of meiosis I is the longest and most complex stage of meiosis. It is subdivided into five successive stages:

  • Leptotene – Chromosomes begin to condense and become visible.

  • Zygotene – Homologous chromosomes pair by synapsis.

  • Pachytene – Crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

  • Diplotene – Homologous chromosomes begin to separate, remaining attached at chiasmata.

  • Diakinesis – Chromosomes become maximally condensed, and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৬) Number of chromosome reduces in -
Anatomy-1.exp:
Meiosis I is the reductional division, during which the chromosome number is reduced from diploid (2n) to haploid (n). This occurs because homologous chromosomes separate during anaphase I.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Mitosis maintains the chromosome number (2n → 2n).

  • Amitosis is a direct cell division without spindle formation and does not normally reduce chromosome number.

  • Meiosis II is an equational division in which sister chromatids separate, but the chromosome number remains haploid (n → n).

Anatomy-1.question: ২৭) Mitosis occurs in -
Anatomy-1.exp:
Mitosis is the mode of cell division that occurs in somatic (body) cells. It produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells and is responsible for growth, tissue repair, and cell replacement.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Primary spermatocyte undergoes meiosis I, not mitosis.

  • Primary oocyte also undergoes meiosis I, beginning during fetal life and completing it only at ovulation.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৮) Meiosis occurs in -
Anatomy-1.exp:
Meiosis begins in the primary spermatocyte, which undergoes meiosis I to form two secondary spermatocytes, followed by meiosis II to produce spermatids.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Spermatogonia divide by mitosis to maintain the germ cell population and produce primary spermatocytes.

  • Oogonia also proliferate by mitosis during fetal life. It is the primary oocyte that enters meiosis I.

  • Somatic cells divide by mitosis, not meiosis.

Anatomy-1.question: ২৯) Which one is not true regarding meiosis?
Anatomy-1.option3: Replication of DNA occurs in between two meiosis
Anatomy-1.option4: Gamets are produced by this process
Anatomy-1.exp:
DNA replication does not occur between meiosis I and meiosis II. DNA is replicated only once, during the S phase before meiosis I. The interval between meiosis I and meiosis II, called interkinesis, has no DNA synthesis.

The other statements are true:

  • Prophase I has five sub-stages: leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, diplotene, and diakinesis.

  • Crossing over occurs during pachytene, and chiasmata become visible during diplotene.

  • Gametes are produced through meiosis.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩০) Which is not a pyrimidine base?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Guanine is a purine base, not a pyrimidine. Purines have a double-ring structure and include:

  • Adenine (A)

  • Guanine (G)

The pyrimidine bases have a single-ring structure and include:

  • Cytosine (C)

  • Thymine (T) – found in DNA

  • Uracil (U) – found in RNA instead of thymine

Anatomy-1.question: ৩১) Nitrogen bases of RNA are/is?
Anatomy-1.exp:
RNA contains four nitrogenous bases:

  • Adenine (A)

  • Guanine (G)

  • Cytosine (C)

  • Uracil (U) (instead of thymine)

Anatomy-1.question: ৩২) Which of the following statements regarding RNA is false?
Anatomy-1.option1: RNA is synthesized from DNA by transcription.
Anatomy-1.option3: RNA contains thymine instead of uracil.
Anatomy-1.option4: mRNA carries genetic information for protein synthesis.
Anatomy-1.exp: RNA contains uracil (U) in place of thymine (T), which is found in DNA. During transcription, RNA is synthesized from a DNA template and contains ribose sugar. mRNA carries the genetic code from DNA to ribosomes, where it directs protein synthesis.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৩) Genetic code is?
Anatomy-1.exp:
The genetic code is considered universal, meaning that the same codon specifies the same amino acid in almost all living organisms. Although there are a few exceptions (e.g., mitochondrial DNA and some protozoa), the genetic code is regarded as universal for standard biological and medical purposes.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Ambiguous – False. The genetic code is unambiguous; each codon specifies only one amino acid.

  • Overlapping – False. The genetic code is non-overlapping; each nucleotide belongs to only one codon during translation.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৪) Which one is true Regarding Telomere?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Telomeres are repetitive DNA sequences located at the ends of linear chromosomes. In humans, they consist of repeated TTAGGG sequences. Their main function is to protect chromosome ends from degradation, end-to-end fusion, and loss of genetic material during DNA replication.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Made of RNA – False. Telomeres are composed of DNA, although telomerase contains an RNA template.

  • Non-essential structure – False. Telomeres are essential for maintaining chromosome stability.

  • Contain genetic code – False. Telomeres are non-coding DNA and do not encode proteins.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৫) Initiation code is -
Anatomy-1.exp:
AUG is the initiation (start) codon for protein synthesis. It signals the ribosome to begin translation and codes for the amino acid methionine (or N-formylmethionine in prokaryotes).

The other options are incorrect:

  • UAA – Stop codon.

  • UAG – Stop codon.

  • GUA – Codes for valine and is not a start codon.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৬) Which one is true Regarding human chromosome?
Anatomy-1.option2: Number in somatic cell is 23 pairs
Anatomy-1.exp:
All the statements are true regarding human chromosomes:

  • The chromosome number is constant for a given species. Humans normally have 46 chromosomes.

  • Somatic cells contain 23 pairs (46 chromosomes).

  • Sperm (and ova) are haploid and contain 23 chromosomes.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৭) Which one is not true regarding philadelphia chromosome?
Anatomy-1.option2: Problem are in 9 and 22 number chromosome
Anatomy-1.exp:
The Philadelphia chromosome results from a reciprocal translocation t(9;22)(q34;q11), creating the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene. It is present in about 90–95% of patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and may also be found in a small proportion of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and occasionally other myeloproliferative neoplasms.

The statement "Prognosis is good if absent" is false. In CML, Philadelphia chromosome-negative disease is uncommon and generally has a less favorable prognosis than Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML because it does not benefit from targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy directed against BCR-ABL1.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৮) Advanced maternal age is most strongly associated with which of the following chromosomal abnormalities?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Advanced maternal age increases the risk of meiotic non-disjunction, particularly during meiosis I, leading to chromosomal aneuploidy. Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) is the most common aneuploidy associated with increasing maternal age.

The other options are less closely related:

  • Turner syndrome (45,X) usually results from sex chromosome nondisjunction but has no strong association with advanced maternal age.

  • Cri-du-chat syndrome is caused by a deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5 (5p−).

  • Achondroplasia is caused by an FGFR3 mutation and is associated with advanced paternal age.

Anatomy-1.question: ৩৯) Which is not a cause of non-disjunction?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate properly during meiosis or mitosis, resulting in aneuploidy. Established risk factors include advanced maternal age and exposure to ionizing radiation, which can disrupt chromosome segregation.

Oral contraceptive pills have no proven association with chromosomal non-disjunction or aneuploidy. Therefore, they are not considered a cause of non-disjunction.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪০) Which relationship is not true?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Turner syndrome is caused by monosomy X (45,X), meaning there is only one X chromosome. It is not a sex chromosome trisomy.

The other associations are correct:

  • Trisomy 21 → Down syndrome

  • Trisomy 13 → Patau syndrome

  • Trisomy 18 → Edwards syndrome

Examples of sex chromosome trisomies include:

  • 47,XXY → Klinefelter syndrome

  • 47,XXX → Triple X syndrome

  • 47,XYY → XYY syndrome

Anatomy-1.question: ৪১) Causes of down syndrome-
Anatomy-1.exp:
Down syndrome can result from three genetic mechanisms:

  • Non-disjunction – The most common cause (about 95% of cases), leading to free trisomy 21.

  • Robertsonian translocation – Accounts for about 3–4% of cases, usually involving chromosomes 14 and 21 or two chromosome 21s.

  • Mosaicism – Occurs in about 1–2% of cases, where some cells have a normal chromosome number while others have trisomy 21.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪২) Which one is not an autosomal dominant disorder?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Neurofibromatosis, achondroplasia, and autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) are all autosomal dominant disorders.

Muscular dystrophies are generally not autosomal dominant. The common forms, such as Duchenne and Becker muscular dystrophy, are X-linked recessive disorders. Thus, the option "Neurogenic Muscular Dystrophy" (although not a standard disease name) is clearly intended to represent a disorder that is not autosomal dominant.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৩) Which one is an autosomal recessive disorder
Anatomy-1.exp: Thalassemia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations affecting the synthesis of α- or β-globin chains. Affected

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৪) Which one is not an xlinked disorder?
Anatomy-1.exp:
von Willebrand disease is not an X-linked disorder. It is usually inherited as an autosomal dominant condition (types 1 and 2), while the rare severe type 3 is autosomal recessive.

The other disorders are X-linked:

  • Fragile X syndrome – X-linked dominant.

  • Duchenne muscular dystrophy – X-linked recessive.

  • Diabetes insipidus (congenital nephrogenic type) – Most commonly X-linked recessive, caused by mutations in the AVPR2 gene.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৫) Indication of chromosome analysis -
Anatomy-1.exp:
Chromosome analysis (karyotyping) is indicated in several clinical situations, including:

  • Recurrent spontaneous abortions, to detect parental balanced translocations or fetal chromosomal abnormalities.

  • Sex determination, especially in patients with ambiguous genitalia or suspected sex chromosome disorders such as Turner syndrome or Klinefelter syndrome.

  • Prenatal diagnosis, particularly when there is advanced maternal age, abnormal fetal screening, or a family history of chromosomal disorders.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৬) Prenatal testing can be done from-
Anatomy-1.exp:
Prenatal genetic testing can be performed using different fetal samples depending on the stage of pregnancy and the clinical indication:

  • Chorionic villus sampling (CVS): Performed at 10–13 weeks of gestation.

  • Amniocentesis: Performed at 15–20 weeks using amniotic fluid.

  • Cordocentesis (Percutaneous umbilical blood sampling): Performed after 18 weeks using fetal cord blood.

All of these samples can be used for prenatal chromosomal and genetic analysis.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৭) Which is not a feature of Klinefelters syndrome?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) is characterized by primary testicular failure, leading to hypergonadotropic hypogonadism. Typical features include gynecomastia, sparse facial and body hair (including reduced pubic hair), small firm testes, infertility, and elevated FSH and LH levels.

Coarctation of the aorta is a classic cardiovascular abnormality associated with Turner syndrome (45,X), not Klinefelter syndrome.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৮) Which one is not a feature of Turner's syndrome?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Turner syndrome (45,X) is characterized by short stature, webbed neck, and a broad shield-shaped chest with widely spaced nipples. Other common features include primary amenorrhea, streak ovaries, infertility, and coarctation of the aorta.

A high-pitched voice is not a characteristic feature of Turner syndrome. It is not considered part of the typical clinical phenotype.

Anatomy-1.question: ৪৯) Which is not a feature of Down syndrome?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Down syndrome (Trisomy 21) is characterized by intellectual disability, congenital heart disease (especially atrioventricular septal defect), and may be associated with umbilical hernia.

The hands in Down syndrome are typically small and broad, with short fingers, a single transverse palmar crease, and clinodactyly of the fifth finger. Therefore, large and narrow hands are not a feature of Down syndrome.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫০) Given a haemophilic husband and unaffected wife-
Anatomy-1.option1: None of their daughter will be affected
Anatomy-1.option2: All of their daughter will carry haemophilic gene
Anatomy-1.option3: His maternal grandfather could have had haemophilia
Anatomy-1.exp:
Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder. A haemophilic husband (XʰY) married to an unaffected, non-carrier wife (XᴴXᴴ) will have:

  • All daughters: XᴴXʰ → carriers, but not affected.

  • All sons: XᴴY → unaffected, because sons inherit the Y chromosome from their father.

The statement that his maternal grandfather could have had haemophilia is also true. A haemophilic maternal grandfather (XʰY) passes his affected X chromosome to all his daughters, making the patient's mother at least a carrier, who can then transmit the affected X chromosome to her son.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫১) Epithelial tissue, not originated from ectoderm-
Anatomy-1.exp:
Most of the epithelium of the genital tract develops from the mesoderm (intermediate mesoderm), as it is derived from the Müllerian (paramesonephric) or Wolffian (mesonephric) ducts.

The other options are derived from ectoderm:

  • Mouth – From the stomodeum (surface ectoderm).

  • Anus – The lower part of the anal canal develops from the proctodeum (ectoderm).

  • Terminal part of the male urethra (navicular fossa) – Derived from surface ectoderm.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫২) Which of the following epithelial linings is derived from the endoderm?
Anatomy-1.exp:
The epithelium of the trachea is derived from the endoderm of the primitive foregut. Similarly, the epithelial lining of the larynx, bronchi, and lungs is also endodermal.

The other options are derived from ectoderm:

  • Epidermis of skin – Surface ectoderm.

  • Lower one-third of the vagina – Urogenital sinus (endoderm is debated in some teaching, making it a less suitable option); better replaced in exams by anal canal below the pectinate line or another ectodermal structure.

  • Corneal epithelium – Surface ectoderm.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৩) Urinary bladder is lined by -
Anatomy-1.exp:
The urinary bladder is lined by transitional epithelium (urothelium), a specialized stratified epithelium that can stretch and recoil as the bladder fills and empties. Its superficial umbrella cells provide an impermeable barrier against urine.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Cuboidal epithelium lines ducts and kidney tubules.

  • Squamous epithelium lines structures such as blood vessels (simple squamous) and the esophagus (stratified squamous).

  • Columnar epithelium lines much of the gastrointestinal tract.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৪) Stratified Squamous epithelium is present in-
Anatomy-1.exp:
The dorsal surface of the tongue is lined predominantly by stratified squamous epithelium, which may be keratinized or non-keratinized depending on the region. This epithelium protects the tongue from mechanical abrasion during mastication.

The other options are lined by different types of epithelium:

  • Trachea – Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.

  • Bronchus – Pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium (becoming simpler in smaller bronchi).

  • Colon – Simple columnar epithelium with abundant goblet cells.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৫) Which one is false regarding epithelial cells?
Anatomy-1.exp:
All the listed statements are true characteristics of epithelial tissue:

  • Closely packed – Epithelial cells are tightly packed with minimal intercellular material.

  • Avascular – Epithelia lack blood vessels and receive nutrients by diffusion from the underlying connective tissue.

  • Got nerve supply – Epithelial tissues are well innervated, making them sensitive to touch, pain, temperature, and other stimuli.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৬) Which one is not true regarding glands?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Sebaceous glands are holocrine glands, not apocrine glands. In holocrine secretion, the entire secretory cell disintegrates and becomes part of the secretion.

The other statements are true:

  • Pancreas is a merocrine gland, releasing its secretions by exocytosis.

  • Mammary glands exhibit apocrine secretion for the lipid component of milk (while the protein component is secreted by the merocrine mechanism).

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৭) Myoepithelial cells-
Anatomy-1.exp:
Myoepithelial cells are specialized contractile cells located between the basement membrane and the secretory or ductal cells of many exocrine glands. Their contraction helps expel glandular secretions into the ducts.

They are present in:

  • Sweat glands

  • Salivary glands

  • Lacrimal glands

They are also found in mammary glands.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৮) Breast is a modified-
Anatomy-1.exp:
The mammary gland (breast) is a modified apocrine sweat gland. It is a specialized exocrine gland that produces and secretes milk after childbirth. Milk proteins are secreted by the merocrine mechanism, whereas milk lipids are secreted by the apocrine mechanism.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Sebaceous gland – Produces sebum by holocrine secretion.

  • Serous gland – Produces watery, enzyme-rich secretions.

  • Mucous gland – Produces mucus.

Anatomy-1.question: ৫৯) Which statement is not true regarding connective tissue?
Anatomy-1.exp:
All the listed statements are true characteristics of connective tissue:

  • Extracellular matrix is the major component of connective tissue and consists of ground substance and fibers.

  • Most connective tissues are vascular and innervated. (Exceptions include cartilage, which is avascular and aneural, and tendons, which are poorly vascularized.)

  • Connective tissue is derived from mesenchyme, which is primarily of mesodermal origin.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬০) Fixed  cells of connective tissue?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Fixed (resident) cells of connective tissue are permanent inhabitants of the tissue. They include fibroblasts, adipocytes (fat cells), and mast cells. These cells remain within the connective tissue and perform structural, storage, and immune functions.

Macrophages may be present as resident (fixed) histiocytes, but they are also capable of migration and are commonly classified as wandering (free) cells in many undergraduate histology texts. Therefore, in this question, the best answer is A + C.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬১) Which is false regarding phagocytes?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Langerhans cells are antigen-presenting dendritic cells found mainly in the epidermis of the skin and mucosal epithelium. They are not pancreatic cells.

The confusion arises because the islets of Langerhans are endocrine cell clusters in the pancreas, but they are not Langerhans cells and are not phagocytes.

The other statements are true:

  • Kupffer cells are resident macrophages of the liver.

  • Osteoclasts are multinucleated phagocytic cells responsible for bone resorption.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬২) Which of the following is not a characteristic of cartilage?
Anatomy-1.exp: Cartilage is an avascular tissue and receives nutrients by diffusion from the surrounding perichondrium or synovial fluid. It also lacks lymphatic vessels and nerves, which contributes to its limited capacity for repair.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৩) Which one is not true?
Anatomy-1.option4: Calcification is frequent in hyaline cartilage
Anatomy-1.exp:
Elastic cartilage is not translucent. It contains abundant elastic fibers, giving it a yellowish, opaque, and flexible appearance. In contrast, hyaline cartilage has a glassy, translucent appearance due to its homogeneous extracellular matrix.

The other statements are true:

  • Cartilage is of three types: hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage.

  • Fibrocartilage lacks a perichondrium.

  • Calcification is relatively common in hyaline cartilage, especially with aging and at sites undergoing endochondral ossification.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৪) Which is not an example of fibrocartilage?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Costal cartilage is composed of hyaline cartilage, which provides flexibility and elasticity to the thoracic cage.

The other structures are composed of fibrocartilage:

  • Intervertebral disc (annulus fibrosus)

  • Symphysis pubis

  • Glenoid labrum (a fibrocartilaginous rim that deepens the glenoid cavity)

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৫) Bone resorbing cell -
Anatomy-1.exp:
Osteoclasts are large, multinucleated cells derived from the monocyte-macrophage lineage. Their primary function is bone resorption, achieved by secreting hydrochloric acid and lysosomal enzymes that dissolve the mineralized bone matrix.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Osteoblasts synthesize and mineralize new bone.

  • Osteocytes are mature bone cells that maintain the bone matrix.

  • Chondroblasts produce cartilage matrix.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৬) Ossified from primary centre-
Anatomy-1.exp:
The primary ossification center develops in the diaphysis (shaft) of a long bone during fetal life. It is the first site where endochondral ossification begins.

The secondary ossification centers appear later, usually after birth, in the epiphyses. The metaphysis is the region between the diaphysis and epiphysis and is not a primary ossification center.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৭) Wrist joint is -
Anatomy-1.exp:
The wrist (radiocarpal) joint is a synovial ellipsoid (condyloid) joint. It allows movement in two planes, including:

  • Flexion and extension

  • Abduction (radial deviation) and adduction (ulnar deviation)

These combined movements also permit circumduction, but rotation does not occur at the wrist joint.

The other options are incorrect:

  • Pivot joint – e.g., proximal radioulnar and atlantoaxial joints.

  • Hinge joint – e.g., elbow and interphalangeal joints.

  • Plane joint – e.g., intercarpal and acromioclavicular joints.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৮) Which one is not true regarding muscle?
Anatomy-1.option3: Diaphragm is an example of smooth muscle
Anatomy-1.exp:
The diaphragm is composed of skeletal (striated) muscle. Although it functions automatically under the control of the respiratory center, it is structurally a skeletal muscle and is supplied by the phrenic nerve.

The other statements are true:

  • Cardiac muscle contains intercalated discs, which facilitate synchronized contraction.

  • Skeletal muscle fibers are multinucleated.

  • Smooth muscle is involuntary and is controlled by the autonomic nervous system.

Anatomy-1.question: ৬৯) Which one is false regarding artery?
Anatomy-1.exp:
Arteries have thick, muscular, and elastic walls to withstand the high pressure generated by the heart. Therefore, the statement that the arterial wall is thin is false.

The other statements are true:

  • Arteries do not collapse because of their thick elastic walls.

  • Valves are absent in normal arteries (except the semilunar valves at the origins of the aorta and pulmonary trunk, which are heart valves).

  • Arteries have a relatively small lumen compared with veins of similar size.

Anatomy-1.question: ৭০) Which one is not a layer of epidermis?
Anatomy-1.exp:
The epidermis consists of five layers (in thick skin):

  • Stratum basale

  • Stratum spinosum

  • Stratum granulosum

  • Stratum lucidum (present only in thick skin)

  • Stratum corneum

The reticular layer is not part of the epidermis. It is the deeper layer of the dermis, composed of dense irregular connective tissue and rich in collagen and elastic fibers.
